---
title: "Week 4 — Turning Data into New Information"
subtitle: "Operators, expressions, evaluation order, and computational transformation"
---

::: {.callout-tip}
## This week's central question

**How does a program transform existing values into new information?**
:::

## Learning goals

By the end of this week, you should be able to:

1. distinguish a **value**, an **operator**, and an **expression**;
2. use arithmetic operators to transform numeric data;
3. predict the result of simple expressions before running code;
4. explain how assignment stores the result of an expression;
5. use parentheses to make evaluation order explicit;
6. identify and repair simple expression errors.

## Connection to Week 3

Last week, we represented information using variables and data types.

This week we ask:

> **How do we transform those represented values into new information?**

## Midterm connection

This week develops two skills that may be assessed in the midterm:

- translating a quantitative relationship into a correct Python expression;
- diagnosing and repairing an incorrect formula or evaluation order.
:::

## Concepts to keep

- operand;
- expression;
- evaluation;

- transformation;
